title: Fixed Open Arc Soundboard and Graduated Pin Nail Violin
description: One newly authored complete unbowed nail-violin-inspired static display. One full thick semicircular wooden-look frame has a genuinely open front and full open underside beneath a separate thin half-round soundboard. Sixteen whole upright blunt metal-look pins root directly in the outer curved frame margin and rise to deliberately graduated display heights; alternating pins retain a small inward upper bend. The board is whole and supported along the inner part of the arc, with a visible interval between its edge and the pin shafts. One whole finite annular-sector lower face is the ground sole. All frame sections, half-disc profile, pin routes and numerical proportions are new, not an old waterphone with its neck removed or kalimba keys turned upright. Unlike the full round enclosed domed pan and tall central tube, the entire instrument body is an open-front wooden arc capped only by its half-round board; unlike a kalimba, there is no box chamber, soundhole, horizontal tine bank or transverse retainer. Eighteen closed editable whole meshes, four constant opaque PBR roles, metres native Z up and horizontal whole-bounds-centred ground origin. One model zero scenes; pins remain subordinate components, never separate assets. Generic instrument-category art, not a measured historical replica or musical layout. No bow, pitch letters, copied labels, rosette, sympathetic strings, historical retaining-wire arrangement or tuned scale reconstructed. No sound, acoustic response, tuning, bow contact, vibration, playability, hand fit, sharpness assessment, balance, manufacture or safety capability made or verified. No rigging, animation or interaction.
